relation_instance_contract: UNORDERED_EVENT_A_KEY || potentially related || UNORDERED_EVENT_B_KEY at Layer 1; Layer 2 evaluates both directed source-to-target checklists and materializes only a final controlled positive relation.

relation_specs.label: PRECONDITION
relation_specs.direction: source event establishes, enables, motivates, or is required for the target event
relation_specs.definition: A directed event-event relation where the source is a prerequisite, enabling condition, motivating circumstance, or necessary setup for the target.
relation_specs.negative_note: Do not choose merely because the source is mentioned earlier. Semantic dependency is required.

relation_specs.label: FALLING_ACTION
relation_specs.direction: source event is connected to a downstream, follow-up, consequence, continuation, aftermath, or elaborating event represented by the target
relation_specs.definition: A directed storyline relation linking an event to a subsequent/downstream consequence, continuation, aftermath, or narratively dependent event when PRECONDITION is not the better interpretation.
relation_specs.negative_note: Do not invert the pair and do not use this as a generic co-occurrence label.

layer01.goal: Extract a high-recall inventory of shortest complete atomic EventStoryLine triggers, audit broad spans, then deterministically construct the closed unordered pair pool without gold relations.
event_mentions: Use the shortest complete lexical trigger, not the full clause or noun phrase.
Strip auxiliaries, negation, subjects, objects, determiners and complements from the event span.
Keep required phrasal particles and all tokenized components of a hyphenated lexical trigger.
Split a broad phrase only when it explicitly contains multiple independently eventive trigger heads.
Extract eventive verbs, participles, infinitives, nouns, nominalizations, processes, occurrences and explicit states.
Preserve repeated mentions as distinct when sentence/token spans differ.
Validate every returned span against source tokens and run a final source-only atomicity audit.
Do not use gold event IDs, counts, spans or relation pairs.
relations: Construct unordered candidate pairs only after the event inventory is validated and closed.

Use exhaustive unordered pairs when the event inventory has at most 25 events; otherwise use the broad hybrid policy covering same/nearby sentences, discourse-cue windows, repeated triggers, and headline-to-body pairs.
Pair construction provides candidate coverage only. It never predicts PRECONDITION or FALLING_ACTION.
Preserve exact event keys and never invent, alter, merge, or swap event spans.
Gold event IDs, gold relation pairs, counts, labels per pair, and gold-derived lexical hints are forbidden.

phases.phase_a3: Final source-only KEEP/DROP/REPLACE/SPLIT atomic span audit.
phases.phase_b: Deterministic adaptive unordered pair construction; no relation-generation LLM call.

layer02.goal: For one fixed source event, classify every candidate target as PRECONDITION, FALLING_ACTION, or NONE in the fixed source-to-target direction.
rules: The request direction is fixed: classify only SOURCE to TARGET. If only TARGET to SOURCE is supported, output NONE; the reverse is evaluated in the target source request.
PRECONDITION means the fixed source directly establishes, enables, motivates, requires, prepares, or sets up the target.
FALLING_ACTION means the target is directly presented as consequence, continuation, aftermath, follow-up, elaboration, or downstream narrative development of the fixed source.
EventStoryLine direction is narrative and annotation-specific; do not replace it with naive physical causality or sentence order.
Headline/body reformulations, legal setup, repeated descriptions, and immediate narrative aftermath may be direct links.
Never infer a transitive relation: A-B and B-C do not justify A-C.
Chronology, co-occurrence, shared topic, and world knowledge are insufficient.
Return every listed target exactly once. Missing targets receive one focused recovery request.
Every positive cites source and target sentence IDs. Evidence formatting is repaired non-destructively and does not erase a valid semantic decision.
Broad false-NONE review and destructive positive verification are disabled.
Only opposite-direction positive conflicts receive compact adjudication.
NONE and invalid outputs never enter Layer 3. OWL-Time remains the seed ontology but does not override source-text relation classification.

layer04.goal: Resolve exact event keys to their native event candidates and preserve the Layer 2 direction.
rules: Both endpoints must be event candidates.
Never swap source and target to improve apparent plausibility.
Reject a relation when either indexed event key cannot be resolved uniquely.

synthetic_relation_examples.text: A permit directly allowed construction to begin.
The bridge collapsed, followed by an emergency inspection.
The headline announced an investigation; the body said officials began examining the incident.
Officials threatened arrest unless the person entered treatment.
A enabled B, and B caused C.
synthetic_relation_examples.explanation: No transitive closure without a direct A-C statement.

negative_examples.text: S2[4:5]::meeting and S5[9:10]::speech occur in the same article
negative_examples.explanation: Co-occurrence alone is not a relation.
A person is not an event endpoint.
A date is not an event endpoint.
The dataset's null key is excluded from the relation vocabulary and evaluation.

negative_examples.text: A and C are connected only through B.

seed_ontology_role: Temporal grounding only; PRECONDITION and FALLING_ACTION remain the controlled normalized benchmark relation labels.
evaluation_scope: All 443 normalized EventStoryLine records (type full + test); null pairs excluded. One-document v1.4 remains the development document before smoke-5.

event_span_examples.rule: Keep the phrasal-verb particle inside the event trigger.
Keep every tokenized component of a hyphenated event trigger.
A multi-token state/event expression may begin with a function word when the complete span is eventive.
Use the atomic eventive noun head.
Split only when both heads independently evoke events.

development_note: v1.6 keeps atomic event extraction and full candidate coverage, while replacing five-way pair batches, broad false-NONE review, and destructive verification with complete source-centric directed checklists.
